acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Mummies family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Tomb Guard, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Bronze-Stitch Threshold Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A taut, dry, fully wrapped guard with a simple headcloth, bronze scarab charms sewn in ordered rows, and a bronze khopesh whose curve matches the crossed-arm stance.

Signature mechanic: Tomb Cross: the Guard crosses its bronze khopesh over one wrapped forearm and turns sideways across a threshold. Bronze charms stitched from wrist to shoulder carry the impact, but the topmost charm pulls one linen seam fully open after the block.
battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable doorway or relic line by crossing khopesh and wrapped forearm, transferring the block through a row of bronze charms that leaves one stitch overloaded.
constructionDimensions: Bandages become directional pressure craft through vane-folded loose ends, hollow bronze charms, sail-stiff collars, perforated masks, and headdress or sarcophagus fins that preserve full wrapping coverage.
Motion reveals force direction through taut strip lines, whistling charm rows, dust streamlines limited to contact, and a still controlling knot, glyph, mask strap, or cartouche seal.
counterplay: Bait the cross with a light attack, move around the weapon side, and cut the final shoulder stitch before the charm row relaxes. Affinity signal: Loose ends pull into one direction while the controlling knot or cartouche becomes perfectly still; entering the lee or cutting that anchor collapses the pressure-driven wrap.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only wind treatment without vane folds, hollow charms, and directional wrapping behavior
Glow-only wind treatment without a still anchor or readable pressure direction
A generic sandstorm that duplicates family-native tomb dust and hides the Mummy
Free-floating bandages that detach from the binding route or expose the whole corpse
identityInvariants: A stiff-limbed human or humanoid silhouette remains wrapped from head to foot, with arms held forward, crossed, guarding, inscribing, or commanding through readable linen tension.
Sun-bleached linen, sand beige, desert ochre, deep gold, lapis blue, and turquoise remain funerary materials and symbols rather than affinity colors.
Linen bandage, dried flesh, gold leaf, lapis, carnelian, bronze, and sandstone grave goods stay materially distinct and retain visible knots, stitches, glyph routes, and breakable seals.
Family-native sand and dust follow disturbed wrappings, tomb movement, and burial objects without becoming Earth or Wind affinity by themselves.
Escalation adds precious thread, glyph density, collars, masks, armor, headdresses, and sarcophagus regalia while the bandages never come off and always explain binding and counterplay.
telegraph: The simple headcloth settles, khopesh and forearm cross, and bronze charms click in order from wrist toward shoulder until the final stitch shines.
